findings.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser drops the post-query `filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` while only setting the GROUPS session attribute when the group-permission set is non-empty, so an admin with no view-users role and no group view permissions receives the realm's complete user list. An admin whose only role is e.g. query-users or manage-group-membership with zero granted groups gets `searchForUserStream` results with no GROUPS attribute and no canView filter: the /users search endpoint returns every user in the realm, leaking emails/usernames to an unauthorized caller (before this diff the filter emptied the result set).

[BUG] The brute-force user search always calls `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and sets the GROUPS attribute only when the set is non-empty, so an admin without any view permission gets an unfiltered stream of all realm users. A fine-grained-authz admin with no view-users role and no granted groups calling the brute-force user search receives all users in the realm instead of an empty result, because neither the GROUPS attribute nor any per-user filter restricts the stream.

[BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects `groupResource.getId()` — the authorization resource's own UUID — while the group's identifier is stored in the resource *name* (per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup naming the resource by group.getId()), so the returned set contains resource IDs that match no group. Consumers (UsersResource.getUsersCount and searchForUser's `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`) filter users against these bogus IDs: even when myadmin holds VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group, the user search and count endpoints return zero results, breaking the exact scenario the new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers claims to cover.

[ADVISORY] resolveGroup performs a full `session.groups().getGroupById` lookup only to return the exact `id` that was passed in, adding a redundant store round-trip per resource creation. Every getOrCreateResource call for a Groups resource pays an unnecessary group-provider lookup (a DB query in the JPA/Map providers) on the admin permission provisioning path; the next change that assumes resolveGroup enriches the name (as resolveUser does via username) will also silently get the raw id instead.

[BUG] Removing the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from searchForUser makes user search return every realm user whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() yields an empty set for a caller who cannot view users. A same-realm admin without view-users/manage-users whose fine-grained grants yield no per-group resources (e.g. cross-realm admin hitting the `!root.isAdminSameRealm()` empty-set branch, or one holding only an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS policy that creates no per-group resource) gets the GROUPS attribute never set, so searchForUserStream returns all realm users unfiltered — a forbidden PII leak the old filter prevented; same shape at BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (lines 147-153), where the attribute is now also set unconditionally, propagating the same hole to the brute-force user listing.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`), so an all-groups permission granting only `view` makes canManage() return true. An admin granted a view-only all-groups scope-permission can create groups, add subgroups and update groups (GroupsResource/GroupResource gate mutations on canManage/requireManage), escalating read access into write access; the test file only exercises a MANAGE all-groups permission (testManageAllGroups), so no test asserts this denial — the missing acceptance criterion is 'view-only all-groups permission must NOT allow group creation/update'.

[BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates only per-group resources (resourceStore.findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) and skips groups covered solely by an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS policy, because it never evaluates the type-level fallback used by hasPermission(groupId, ...) for groups with no individual resource. An admin whose only grant is an all-groups view-members policy gets an empty group-ID set, so the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set in UsersResource.searchForUser: users that canViewByGroup/canView(user) says they may view are silently absent from the user-search results, and conversely the unfiltered stream (per the removed canView filter) exposes users they must not see.

[ADVISORY] MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() lazily assigns the non-volatile instance field `groupPermissions` without synchronization, diverging from the pattern risk in a shared/admin session context where MgmtPermissions instances can be reached from concurrent admin requests. Under concurrent admin requests sharing a permissions instance, two GroupPermissionsV2 objects can be constructed and one thread operates on an evaluator whose cached policy decisions (root.evaluatePermission caches) diverge; next maintainer touching this class must also reason about which of users()/clients()/groups() lazy fields are thread-safe.

[BUG] searchForUser drops the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and relies solely on the non-empty UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, so a caller with no global view permission and no group permissions gets an unfiltered stream of every realm user. An admin holding only query-users, or only fine-grained per-user authorization grants (Users resource type) now receives the full realm user list (usernames, emails) from GET /users — the endpoint previously enforced the view filter per user, so this is a data-exposure regression; the GROUPS attribute path only restricts results when the set is non-empty, and user-level grants never enter it.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (realm-wide) evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, granting manage on the mere VIEW scope, contradicting the interface javadoc added in this same diff which requires MANAGE. An admin with only a VIEW permission on the all-groups resource passes requireManage() and can create groups and modify group configuration — a privilege escalation relative to the documented contract; the same asymmetry is absent from canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks MANAGE only.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ProviderEventListener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)` on GroupRemovedEvent when the authz feature is enabled. With the fine-grained authz feature enabled and the V2 evaluator active (MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2), deleting a group fires GroupRemovedEvent and the cleanup path throws UnsupportedOperationException, failing the group-removal operation with a 500 instead of completing the delete.

[ADVISORY] The V2 evaluator stubs out the entire GroupPermissionManagement surface (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission) with UnsupportedOperationException, so the PR ships the Groups resource type without any writer/operator path for managing those permissions under V2. Admin endpoints that read or toggle group permission resources (admin-ui-ext permission management UI, realm export of group permissions) return HTTP 500 whenever V2 is active, leaving operators unable to inspect or disable group permissions — the new GROUPS resource type is inert-with-crash rather than usable.

[ADVISORY] Moving the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check from inside the event handler to listener-registration time changes registration semantics and is not traceable to the stated intent of adding a Groups resource type and scopes. The listener is now permanently bound (or not) at startup based on the feature check, so environments where the feature evaluation is done after this registration point (or via the feature-disabled-by-default startup ordering) silently skip all role/group permission cleanup; also the retained GroupRemovedEvent branch calls a V2-unsupported method (see related finding), so this drift makes the diff harder to reason about rather than safer.

[ADVISORY] The V1 (legacy) canViewMembers was broadened from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` and requireViewMembers rerouted through it, changing existing fine-grained-authz behavior outside the PR's stated scope. Existing deployments using the legacy evaluator gain new access for admins who only hold manage-members on a group: those admins can now also view members of those groups (member lists visible where previously Forbidden), a silent permission broadening shipped under a PR titled 'add Groups resource type and scopes' with no requirement cited.

[ADVISORY] Rewriting ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse to try-with-resources is unrelated housekeeping with no traceability to the 'Add Groups resource type and scopes' intent. Bundling unrelated test-framework changes into an authz-scoped PR means a revert or backport of the permission work drags the shared test utility along (or vice versa), and any behavioral difference in response-close semantics for non-201 responses now has to be debugged inside a security-focused change.

[BUG] searchForUser removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter and relies solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute being honored by the user storage provider, so an admin with only QUERY_USERS (no view-users role and no group permissions) now receives the full user list. An admin with query-users role and no view permission gets groupIds empty, the GROUPS attribute is never set, searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm unfiltered — emails and attributes of users they are not permitted to see leak via GET /users; the same leak occurs whenever a user-federation provider (e.g., a custom UserStorageProvider or LDAP store that ignores the GROUPS attribute) serves the search, since the in-code filter that previously backstopped those providers is gone.

[BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource's own UUID) into the set that callers put in UserModel.GROUPS, but searchForUserStream matches that set against user group IDs, which correspond to the resource *name* (resolveGroup creates resources named by group.getId()). For an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on specific groups via V2, the set placed in UserModel.GROUPS contains authz resource UUIDs that never equal any user's group IDs, so the user search silently returns zero users — admins with legitimate per-group member permissions see an empty user list while direct per-user access (canView(user)) succeeds, an inconsistent and silent denial.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only scans per-group resources for VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS and ignores a type-level (all-groups) policy, while per-group canViewMembers falls back to the type-level resource in hasPermission when the per-group resource is absent. An admin granted an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS policy (type-level 'Groups' resource) can fetch any individual user by ID — canViewMembers(group) hits the type-resource fallback — but the bulk user search and getUsersCount return nothing, because the ID-collection path never reflects the type-level grant; the list and the direct-read paths disagree.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission overloads the empty-set sentinel to mean both 'global view, no restriction needed' (when users().canView()) and 'no group grants exist' (fallback paths return Collections.emptySet()), which callers cannot distinguish. Callers like UsersResource.searchForUser treat empty set as 'do not set the GROUPS attribute' i.e. unrestricted search; any future caller (or the removed canManage() branch: previously canManage() also returned empty/unrestricted, now falls through to the restricted group scan) that reads empty as 'no permission' instead of 'unrestricted' will either leak the full user list or silently deny; the removal of the users().canManage() guard in this same method also silently changes search/count results for admins holding manage-users without view-users in non-composite role setups.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from eight inherited GroupPermissionManagement/evaluator methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions) that existing V1-era admin endpoints and the fine-grained permission UI still call through the same GroupPermissionEvaluator interface. When the V2 evaluator is wired in (MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()), any admin-console or REST path that reads or writes group permission listings — the management-permissions toggle endpoints in GroupResource/GroupsResource — turns a normal request into a 500 via UnsupportedOperationException instead of degrading or returning a typed error, breaking existing clients the moment the feature is enabled.

[BUG] searchForUser now sets the GROUPS session attribute unconditionally whenever groupIds is non-empty, dropping the old `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard, and never applies a per-user canView filter, so a caller with view-users permission whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission somehow returns non-empty (e.g., a UserPermissionsV2 where users().canView() is false but an admin role check elsewhere passed) gets the brute-force user list silently restricted to those groups. A realm admin who legitimately can view all users sees a truncated brute-force status list when the evaluator's role check and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's canView() preconditions disagree (users().canView() checks VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS roles while other gates check different role sets), yielding inconsistent results between the brute-force screen and the main users screen.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (global) grants full group-manage rights to callers holding only the VIEW scope, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) instead of requiring MANAGE. An admin granted only view-all-groups permission can pass requireManage() and create/update/delete any group, escalating read-only access to write access across the realm; this contradicts the interface javadoc which says canManage() requires MANAGE.

[BUG] The per-user usersEvaluator::canView post-filter was silently removed from searchForUser, replacing it with a group-ID-only session attribute, so user-level (Users resource) VIEW/MANAGE grants no longer contribute to search results. An admin authorized via a permission on an individual user resource (not via any group) previously saw that user in GET /users search; after this change getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns only group-resource grants, the session attribute omits them, and their previously visible users vanish from search results — a silent authorization-surface regression with no accompanying intent statement.

[BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource's own ID) rather than the resource's name (which per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource is the group ID), so the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute is populated with resource IDs, not group IDs. If resource IDs are not identical to group IDs, the downstream search filtering on UserModel.GROUPS matches no real group, and an admin with only VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants sees an empty user list instead of the members of the groups they are authorized for; the same asymmetry is visible in hasPermission(), which looks resources up by name (findByName(server, groupId)) — the write side and read side of this contract use different identifiers.

[BUG] The `!auth.users().canView()` guard was dropped, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is now consulted unconditionally, but the empty-set fallthrough means a caller with neither canView nor any group permission still gets no UserModel.GROUPS attribute set and the brute-force user search runs completely unfiltered. A fine-grained-authorized admin with zero granted groups receives the full brute-force user list (all realm users with their brute-force status), the same unrestricted result as a fully privileged admin — the permission narrowing the old code aimed to preserve is silently a no-op for the no-grants case in both old and new code, and this iteration cemented it while touching exactly these lines.

[ADVISORY] The V1 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() shortcut was narrowed from `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()` to `root.users().canView()` only, while every caller of the old method was rewritten in the same diff to call the new one, so the effective contract of all four UsersResource count branches changed without any statement of which behavior was accepted. Admins holding manage-only user permissions (e.g. via MANAGE scope on the Users resource without VIEW) now take the group-scoped path in getUsersCount, and since canView() does not cover them, their counts can silently differ from their pre-change counts; whoever bites this is a fine-grained-authz admin comparing user totals across a Keycloak upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check was moved from per-event evaluation to listener-registration time, so the cleanup listener is now permanently bound to the feature state at whatever moment registerListener runs. In any deployment path where registerListener is invoked before feature resolution (or where the feature flag is read from a source that changes between startup and operation), role-removal and group-removal events stop cleaning up the corresponding authorization policies, leaving orphaned permission resources that keep stale grants alive after the originating role/group is deleted.

[BUG] searchForUser removes the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` guard and treats an empty group-ids set as full access, so an admin with no view permission at all receives the unscoped user list. An admin holding only query-users (or any role that passes requireQuery but not view) whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (no global canView, no group view-membership grants) now gets every user in the realm returned with full representation, where the old code returned an empty/filtered stream — a direct user-enumeration and PII disclosure bypass of the view-users check.

[BUG] searchForUser drops the `if (!auth.users().canView())` gate and any per-result authorization filter, so brute-force status for all realm users is returned whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is empty. An admin without view-users and without any group view-membership grant previously got no results (the GROUPS attribute was only set when permissions existed and canView() gated everything); now the same admin receives the full brute-force status stream including login failure timestamps for every user in the realm.

[BUG] canManage() grants manage-level group authority from a VIEW-only scope grant: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` An admin granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource (view-only fine-grained permission, matching canView()'s identical check) is indistinguishable from a MANAGE grant at the canManage() level, so view-only admins can create, update, and delete groups — privilege escalation from view to manage.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(groupId, ...) evaluates only the group-named resource when one exists, skipping the type-level "all-groups" resource check, so a type-level grant is silently ignored for groups that already have a per-group resource. An admin with MANAGE on all-groups gets Forbidden when managing a group whose per-group resource was previously created (e.g., by an earlier scope permission), while the same grant works for groups without one — the testManageAllGroups case only exercises the no-resource path, so this authorization asymmetry is untested and bites admins inconsistently during rolling permission setups.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() now returns an empty set for callers lacking canView(), and every caller (UsersResource.getUsersCount, searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) interprets an empty set as "no restriction", making the empty set a dual-meaning sentinel for both full-access and no-access. Any future caller that forgets the separate canView() pre-check gets unrestricted results, and the getUsersCount paths at UsersResource lines 398/425/431 pass the empty set straight into getUsersCount, returning the total realm user count to admins with zero view permission — the count endpoint now leaks realm size where the old getGroupsWithViewPermission-served path denied it.

[BUG] searchForUser drops the `!auth.users().canView()` guard AND removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter, so filtering now depends entirely on the GROUPS session attribute, which is never set when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set. An admin with no view-users role and no group view permissions gets an empty group set, the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set, and searchForUserStream returns the realm's full user list unfiltered — a privilege escalation leaking all users (the old code caught this case with the canView post-filter).

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() reuses the empty set as a sentinel with three contradictory meanings: 'caller can view all users' (canView branch), 'cross-realm admin' (returns empty), and 'no groups granted' (loop adds nothing). Callers like UsersResource.getUsersCount (lines 398, 425, 432) cannot distinguish 'unrestricted' from 'restricted to zero groups', so a cross-realm or permission-less admin gets the same empty-set input that a full-view admin gets; the next maintainer of any store provider implementing getUsersCount(realm, Set) will guess the semantics wrong and either leak or over-restrict counts.

[ADVISORY] All three getUsersCount call sites changed from getGroupsWithViewPermission to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, but no test in the diff exercises the count endpoints for a group-restricted admin. I checked the test-shaped files in this diff (tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and test-framework ApiUtil.java); neither calls getUsersCount or asserts a count under group-scoped permissions, so a regression in count-vs-search consistency (e.g. count says 5, search returns 1) ships unnoticed to realm admins paging user lists.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 grants user-search visibility (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) only for VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes on group resources, but canView(GroupModel) grants group visibility on VIEW/MANAGE scopes — an admin granted plain VIEW on a group can open that group in the UI yet its members never appear in user searches or counts. An operator who grants 'view' on a group (the natural scope to let someone see a group) silently gets an empty member list via the users endpoint; no test in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest creates a group permission with only VIEW/MANAGE and then asserts users-search behavior, so this inconsistency is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new switch in getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types, but this new default branch is not triggered by any test in the diff. I checked GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest (the only test file added); it never calls getOrCreateResource with an invalid resourceType, so a regression that maps a valid type string into the default branch (e.g. a typo'd constant) would surface as a raw 500 to admin clients instead of being caught by a test asserting the intended error contract.

[ADVISORY] The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved from inside the ProviderEventListener to wrap the listener registration entirely — a behavioral change on the feature-disabled path with no test in the diff exercising a feature-disabled server. I checked GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest and KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig usage in the diff — every test runs with the feature enabled (the config class exists precisely to enable it), so if the hoisted check accidentally reads the profile before bootstrap completes (returning false and silently skipping listener registration), stale group permission resources would never be cleaned up on role/group deletion and no test would notice.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants full group management to callers holding only the VIEW scope, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) instead of MANAGE alone. An admin granted a view-only all-groups permission can create, update, and delete groups and map roles to them (GroupResource/GroupsResource only call canManage/canView before mutating), an authorization bypass versus the documented contract that canManage requires the MANAGE scope — note the per-group canManage(GroupModel) overload correctly checks only MANAGE, so the global and per-group paths disagree.

[BUG] searchForUser removes the application-level `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and relies entirely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute being honored by the user provider, but the attribute is only set when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns non-empty. For a group-scoped admin whose user storage provider does not implement the GROUPS attribute filter (any custom/UserStorageProvider federation that ignores unknown attributes), searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm with no downstream permission filter, exposing users the admin has no permission to view; previously the stream-level canView filter caught this.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission() looks up per-group resources via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), but pre-existing fine-grained group resources in upgraded realms are named with the V1 convention "group.resource.<id>" (GroupPermissions.getGroupResourceName), so the lookup by raw group id misses them. Realms upgraded from the V1 admin-fine-grained-authz model silently lose their existing per-group permission grants when evaluated through V2 (hasPermission falls through to the all-groups policy and returns false), so admins who could manage specific groups are locked out with no error, warning, or migration/backfill step for renaming resources.

[ADVISORY] The new code sets the GROUPS attribute unconditionally (whenever non-empty) instead of only when auth.users().canView() is false, and it drops the canView gate entirely from the search path. For callers who can view all users, the GROUPS attribute is now set on the session only when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() happens to return entries (e.g., V2 admins holding an explicit all-groups VIEW permission), narrowing the brute-force user search to that group list even though the caller has realm-wide view rights — a behavior change on the same request path with no V1/V2 distinction.

[BUG] Removing the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter makes the search stream completely unfiltered whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (caller lacks users().canView() AND has no group view-members grants). An admin holding only the query-users role (who previously got an empty, permission-filtered result) now receives full UserRepresentations of every user in the realm, including emails and attributes — a silent exposure of data the previous code guaranteed was filtered, with no error raised.

[BUG] The rewritten searchForUser drops the authorization narrowing entirely: when groupIds is empty (no view-users and no group permissions) the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set, yet searchForUserStream is invoked with no subsequent permission filter, returning every realm user. A brute-force listing endpoint served to an admin without user-view permission returns all users' brute-force status unfiltered, where the old code constrained results via the group permission attribute path — silent over-visibility with a success response.

[BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource's internal ID) instead of the group ID (the resource name, which the sibling hasPermission() lookup `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` confirms is the group ID) into the granted set. The collected IDs are set as the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and compared against real group IDs during user search, so an admin granted view-members on specific groups gets a set of unmatched resource UUIDs and the user-search filter silently matches nothing — the admin sees zero users despite valid permissions, with no error or log.

This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
