adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the post-query `filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` and now only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. That change could broaden the returned stream when the caller lacks global user-view and has no group-based view permissions, depending on how `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and/or `toRepresentation(...)` enforce authorization (not shown in the diff). The finding’s specific claim that this definitively returns the complete realm user list cannot be proven from the diff alone, but the removed filter + conditional GROUPS attribute is a concrete, diff-grounded security/correctness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The brute-force user search always calls `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and sets the GROUPS attribute only when the set is non-empty, so an admin without any view permission gets an unfiltered stream of all realm users. A fine-grained-authz admin with no view-users role and no granted groups calling the brute-force user search receives all users in the realm instead of an empty result, because neither the GROUPS attribute nor any per-user filter restricts the stream.

adjudication.rationale: In `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the diff now always computes `groupIds = auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `!groupIds.isEmpty()`, then returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` without any `usersEvaluator::canView` filtering. If the caller cannot globally view users and has no group IDs with view-members/manage-members permission, `groupIds` is empty so no GROUPS constraint is applied at all, and nothing else in this method restricts the returned stream. The same pattern/regression is also visible in `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` where the previous `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed. This can expose all users to a caller who should see none.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects `groupResource.getId()` — the authorization resource's own UUID — while the group's identifier is stored in the resource *name* (per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup naming the resource by group.getId()), so the returned set contains resource IDs that match no group. Consumers (UsersResource.getUsersCount and searchForUser's `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`) filter users against these bogus IDs: even when myadmin holds VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group, the user search and count endpoints return zero results, breaking the exact scenario the new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers claims to cover.
matched_golden_ids: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is returning the authorization resource UUID (groupResource.getId()) even though permission evaluation and downstream filtering expect actual group IDs stored as the resource name (group.getId()). This leads to returned IDs that don’t match groups used in UserModel.GROUPS and user count/search filters, causing incorrect results for per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] resolveGroup performs a full `session.groups().getGroupById` lookup only to return the exact `id` that was passed in, adding a redundant store round-trip per resource creation. Every getOrCreateResource call for a Groups resource pays an unnecessary group-provider lookup (a DB query in the JPA/Map providers) on the admin permission provisioning path; the next change that assumes resolveGroup enriches the name (as resolveUser does via username) will also silently get the raw id instead.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema, the newly added resolveGroup(KeycloakSession, String) does session.groups().getGroupById(realm, id) and then returns group == null ? null : group.getId() (i.e., effectively the same id input). This introduces an extra group-provider lookup on the getOrCreateResource path (switch case GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE -> resolveGroup) without enriching the resource name beyond the id; the lookup mainly serves existence validation. This is a concrete perf/maintainability concern visible in the diff, but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from searchForUser makes user search return every realm user whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() yields an empty set for a caller who cannot view users. A same-realm admin without view-users/manage-users whose fine-grained grants yield no per-group resources (e.g. cross-realm admin hitting the `!root.isAdminSameRealm()` empty-set branch, or one holding only an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS policy that creates no per-group resource) gets the GROUPS attribute never set, so searchForUserStream returns all realm users unfiltered — a forbidden PII leak the old filter prevented; same shape at BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (lines 147-153), where the attribute is now also set unconditionally, propagating the same hole to the brute-force user listing.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the only explicit per-user authorization gate: `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` directly into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction is setting `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. But `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (see `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and new `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`) can legitimately return an empty set for callers who *do not* have global user-view (e.g., `!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, `server == null`, or no matching group permissions). In those cases, `UserModel.GROUPS` is not set and the user-search query is no longer post-filtered by `usersEvaluator::canView`, so the method can return users that the evaluator would previously have excluded. This is a behavior/security regression introduced by this diff. (The brute-force resource did not have that per-user filter before, so the strongest verifiable regression is in `UsersResource`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`), so an all-groups permission granting only `view` makes canManage() return true. An admin granted a view-only all-groups scope-permission can create groups, add subgroups and update groups (GroupsResource/GroupResource gate mutations on canManage/requireManage), escalating read access into write access; the test file only exercises a MANAGE all-groups permission (testManageAllGroups), so no test asserts this denial — the missing acceptance criterion is 'view-only all-groups permission must NOT allow group creation/update'.
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly treats VIEW as sufficient by calling hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing users with only VIEW to pass canManage() and gain write access. This is the same issue described in the golden comment, including the correct contrast with canView() behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates only per-group resources (resourceStore.findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) and skips groups covered solely by an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS policy, because it never evaluates the type-level fallback used by hasPermission(groupId, ...) for groups with no individual resource. An admin whose only grant is an all-groups view-members policy gets an empty group-ID set, so the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set in UsersResource.searchForUser: users that canViewByGroup/canView(user) says they may view are silently absent from the user-search results, and conversely the unfiltered stream (per the removed canView filter) exposes users they must not see.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the loop iterates authorization *resources* via `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. But callers (e.g. `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`) store this set into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, which is expected to contain **group IDs** (the same IDs used by membership filtering), not authorization-resource internal IDs. This is inconsistent with the prior implementation which added `groupResource.getName()` (effectively the group identifier). Additionally, if access is granted only through a type-level “all-groups” permission, `findByType` does not enumerate realm groups (only existing authz resources), so the method cannot return the actual group IDs covered by that global grant. Combined with the diff removing the `usersEvaluator::canView` filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, incorrect/empty `UserModel.GROUPS` can lead to missing users or overly broad results depending on how `searchForUserStream` interprets the attribute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() lazily assigns the non-volatile instance field `groupPermissions` without synchronization, diverging from the pattern risk in a shared/admin session context where MgmtPermissions instances can be reached from concurrent admin requests. Under concurrent admin requests sharing a permissions instance, two GroupPermissionsV2 objects can be constructed and one thread operates on an evaluator whose cached policy decisions (root.evaluatePermission caches) diverge; next maintainer touching this class must also reason about which of users()/clients()/groups() lazy fields are thread-safe.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an unsynchronized lazy-initialized field in `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` (`if (groupPermissions != null) return groupPermissions; groupPermissions = new GroupPermissionsV2(...)`), but the finding’s core claim depends on unshown assumptions: that `MgmtPermissionsV2` instances are shared across concurrent admin requests and that constructing two evaluators could cause “cached policy decisions” to diverge. Neither shared-instance concurrency nor any caching behavior of `root.evaluatePermission` is evidenced in this diff. Also, the code matches the existing lazy-init pattern already used for `userPermissions`/`clientPermissions` in the same class rather than “diverging from the pattern.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser drops the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and relies solely on the non-empty UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, so a caller with no global view permission and no group permissions gets an unfiltered stream of every realm user. An admin holding only query-users, or only fine-grained per-user authorization grants (Users resource type) now receives the full realm user list (usernames, emails) from GET /users — the endpoint previously enforced the view filter per user, so this is a data-exposure regression; the GROUPS attribute path only restricts results when the set is non-empty, and user-level grants never enter it.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-user authorization guard `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` directly into `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, the query-scoping mechanism via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` is only applied when `groupIds` is non-empty (`if (!groupIds.isEmpty()) ...`). Therefore, for callers who lack global view (`usersEvaluator.canView()` false) and have no group-based view permission (empty `groupIds`), this method no longer applies *any* filtering at this call site and will request the full stream from the user store. Previously, even when no GROUPS attribute was set, the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` would prevent exposure. The same pattern is also applied in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)` (unfiltered store search, GROUPS set only when non-empty), reinforcing the regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (realm-wide) evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, granting manage on the mere VIEW scope, contradicting the interface javadoc added in this same diff which requires MANAGE. An admin with only a VIEW permission on the all-groups resource passes requireManage() and can create groups and modify group configuration — a privilege escalation relative to the documented contract; the same asymmetry is absent from canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks MANAGE only.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, the realm-wide `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a principal with only the `VIEW` scope on the all-groups (type-level) resource would satisfy `canManage()` and therefore `requireManage()`. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` which correctly requires `MANAGE` only (`hasPermission(group.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`), and it effectively collapses “view all groups” into “manage all groups” for the realm-wide check. That is a concrete authorization correctness/security issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ProviderEventListener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)` on GroupRemovedEvent when the authz feature is enabled. With the fine-grained authz feature enabled and the V2 evaluator active (MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2), deleting a group fires GroupRemovedEvent and the cleanup path throws UnsupportedOperationException, failing the group-removal operation with a 500 instead of completing the delete.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener` registers a `ProviderEventListener` (when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) that, on `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent`, calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). In the same diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` is overridden to return a `GroupPermissionsV2` instance (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), and `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, under the feature flag with V2 permissions in use, handling a group-removed event will throw at runtime, plausibly breaking group deletion/cleanup with a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The V2 evaluator stubs out the entire GroupPermissionManagement surface (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission) with UnsupportedOperationException, so the PR ships the Groups resource type without any writer/operator path for managing those permissions under V2. Admin endpoints that read or toggle group permission resources (admin-ui-ext permission management UI, realm export of group permissions) return HTTP 500 whenever V2 is active, leaving operators unable to inspect or disable group permissions — the new GROUPS resource type is inert-with-crash rather than usable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably adds `GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions` and explicitly overrides the `GroupPermissionManagement` methods (`isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (“Not supported in V2”). It also wires V2 to use this evaluator via `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`. However, the claim that specific admin endpoints (admin-ui-ext permission UI / realm export) will hit these methods and return HTTP 500 is not shown in this diff, so the concrete crash scenario can’t be fully verified from the provided changes alone. Still, the diff clearly ships a V2 groups permissions implementation where the management surface is non-functional and will hard-fail if exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check from inside the event handler to listener-registration time changes registration semantics and is not traceable to the stated intent of adding a Groups resource type and scopes. The listener is now permanently bound (or not) at startup based on the feature check, so environments where the feature evaluation is done after this registration point (or via the feature-disabled-by-default startup ordering) silently skip all role/group permission cleanup; also the retained GroupRemovedEvent branch calls a V2-unsupported method (see related finding), so this drift makes the diff harder to reason about rather than safer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` moves `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` from inside `onEvent(...)` to outside, gating listener *registration* (`if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { manager.register(...) }`). This is a real, diff-grounded semantics change: when the feature is disabled at registration time, the listener will never be registered and will never run, whereas previously the listener was always registered and the feature check happened per-event. The finding’s claims about environments where feature evaluation happens “after this registration point” or startup ordering effects are plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s better treated as a concrete design/semantics concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The V1 (legacy) canViewMembers was broadened from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` and requireViewMembers rerouted through it, changing existing fine-grained-authz behavior outside the PR's stated scope. Existing deployments using the legacy evaluator gain new access for admins who only hold manage-members on a group: those admins can now also view members of those groups (member lists visible where previously Forbidden), a silent permission broadening shipped under a PR titled 'add Groups resource type and scopes' with no requirement cited.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably broadens legacy (V1) authorization: in `GroupPermissions`, `canViewMembers(GroupModel)` changes from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` (lines around `return hasPermission(...)`), and `requireViewMembers` is rerouted to `canViewMembers(group)` (previously it called `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`). This means principals granted only `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` on a group will now pass `requireViewMembers` and be able to view group members where they previously would be forbidden—i.e., a silent permission broadening/security behavior change introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rewriting ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse to try-with-resources is unrelated housekeeping with no traceability to the 'Add Groups resource type and scopes' intent. Bundling unrelated test-framework changes into an authz-scoped PR means a revert or backport of the permission work drags the shared test utility along (or vice versa), and any behavioral difference in response-close semantics for non-201 responses now has to be debugged inside a security-focused change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an independent change in `test-framework/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testframework/util/ApiUtil.java`, refactoring `handleCreatedResponse` from explicit `response.close()` to `try (response) { ... }`. This is not directly tied to the authz/groups-resource-type changes elsewhere in the PR and could complicate cherry-picks/reverts/backports by coupling a shared test utility refactor with security/permission logic changes. The note about response-close semantics also matches the diff: with try-with-resources the response will be closed even if the `assertEquals(201, ...)` fails, whereas previously a failing assertion would skip `response.close()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter and relies solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute being honored by the user storage provider, so an admin with only QUERY_USERS (no view-users role and no group permissions) now receives the full user list. An admin with query-users role and no view permission gets groupIds empty, the GROUPS attribute is never set, searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm unfiltered — emails and attributes of users they are not permitted to see leak via GET /users; the same leak occurs whenever a user-federation provider (e.g., a custom UserStorageProvider or LDAP store that ignores the GROUPS attribute) serves the search, since the in-code filter that previously backstopped those providers is gone.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource#searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit authorization backstop `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly (wrapped only by `toRepresentation(...)`). The only remaining restriction is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. For a caller who can `requireQuery()` (e.g., has `QUERY_USERS`) but has no global view/manage and no group member-view permissions, `groupIds` will be empty, the session attribute is not set, and the underlying `searchForUserStream` is invoked without any enforced per-user visibility filter in this method. This is a security-sensitive regression compared to the previous code, and it also makes correctness depend on all user providers honoring the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute (which this method no longer compensates for).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource's own UUID) into the set that callers put in UserModel.GROUPS, but searchForUserStream matches that set against user group IDs, which correspond to the resource *name* (resolveGroup creates resources named by group.getId()). For an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on specific groups via V2, the set placed in UserModel.GROUPS contains authz resource UUIDs that never equal any user's group IDs, so the user search silently returns zero users — admins with legitimate per-group member permissions see an empty user list while direct per-user access (canView(user)) succeeds, an inconsistent and silent denial.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(... GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. However, group resources are resolved/created with their *name* equal to the actual Keycloak group id (`AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`, which is used as the resource name in `getOrCreateResource`). The non-V2 implementation correctly uses `groupResource.getName()` when collecting granted group identifiers. Callers (e.g. `UsersResource.searchForUser` / `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`) store this set under `UserModel.GROUPS`, which is meant to contain group IDs; supplying authz resource UUIDs will not match user group IDs, leading to incorrect filtering (likely empty results) for admins relying on per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only scans per-group resources for VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS and ignores a type-level (all-groups) policy, while per-group canViewMembers falls back to the type-level resource in hasPermission when the per-group resource is absent. An admin granted an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS policy (type-level 'Groups' resource) can fetch any individual user by ID — canViewMembers(group) hits the type-resource fallback — but the bulk user search and getUsersCount return nothing, because the ID-collection path never reflects the type-level grant; the list and the direct-read paths disagree.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and, when permission matches, adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. But callers (`UsersResource#getUsersCount`, `UsersResource#searchForUser`, `BruteForceUsersResource#searchForUser`) pass this set into user search/count as `UserModel.GROUPS`, which (by intent and prior code naming) expects *group IDs*, not authorization *resource IDs*. Additionally, the V2 `hasPermission(..)` method explicitly falls back to the type-level (all-groups) resource when a per-group resource is not found, so a type-level `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` grant can make `canViewMembers(group)` true for arbitrary groups, while `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` does not expand that into the corresponding group IDs for bulk search/count. This makes direct per-group checks and bulk listing/count paths disagree, matching the finding’s inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission overloads the empty-set sentinel to mean both 'global view, no restriction needed' (when users().canView()) and 'no group grants exist' (fallback paths return Collections.emptySet()), which callers cannot distinguish. Callers like UsersResource.searchForUser treat empty set as 'do not set the GROUPS attribute' i.e. unrestricted search; any future caller (or the removed canManage() branch: previously canManage() also returned empty/unrestricted, now falls through to the restricted group scan) that reads empty as 'no permission' instead of 'unrestricted' will either leak the full user list or silently deny; the removal of the users().canManage() guard in this same method also silently changes search/count results for admins holding manage-users without view-users in non-composite role setups.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` return `Collections.emptySet()` in multiple distinct situations: (a) “no restriction needed” when `root.users().canView()` is true (per new javadoc and `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` / `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`), and also (b) “no grants/cannot evaluate” on fallback paths (`!isAdminSameRealm`, `server == null`, or simply no matching group permissions found). Callers in this diff treat an empty set as “don’t set `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute” (see `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), which results in calling `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` without any group restriction. This is made riskier by the same diff removing the explicit `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and similar stream simplification in `BruteForceUsersResource`), so an empty set due to “no grants” can translate into an unrestricted user search rather than “return none”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from eight inherited GroupPermissionManagement/evaluator methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions) that existing V1-era admin endpoints and the fine-grained permission UI still call through the same GroupPermissionEvaluator interface. When the V2 evaluator is wired in (MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()), any admin-console or REST path that reads or writes group permission listings — the management-permissions toggle endpoints in GroupResource/GroupsResource — turns a normal request into a 500 via UnsupportedOperationException instead of degrading or returning a typed error, breaking existing clients the moment the feature is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` to return `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)` (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java), and `GroupPermissionsV2` overrides multiple inherited `GroupPermissionManagement` methods to immediately `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc. in services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java). The diff also contains at least one concrete caller of a now-unsupported method: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` invokes `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` on certain provider events (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). If V2 permissions are active, that call path would throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, producing a 500-style failure rather than a typed/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser now sets the GROUPS session attribute unconditionally whenever groupIds is non-empty, dropping the old `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard, and never applies a per-user canView filter, so a caller with view-users permission whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission somehow returns non-empty (e.g., a UserPermissionsV2 where users().canView() is false but an admin role check elsewhere passed) gets the brute-force user list silently restricted to those groups. A realm admin who legitimately can view all users sees a truncated brute-force status list when the evaluator's role check and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's canView() preconditions disagree (users().canView() checks VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS roles while other gates check different role sets), yielding inconsistent results between the brute-force screen and the main users screen.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard and the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, but the core claim about “a caller who can view all users getting silently restricted because `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns non-empty” is not supported by the diff. In the updated `GroupPermissionEvaluator` contract and its implementations (`GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` and `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`), the method returns `Collections.emptySet()` when `root.users().canView()` is true, so a global viewer should not get `UserModel.GROUPS` set at all. The alleged mismatch scenario (global view granted but `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` still non-empty) is speculative and not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (global) grants full group-manage rights to callers holding only the VIEW scope, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) instead of requiring MANAGE. An admin granted only view-all-groups permission can pass requireManage() and create/update/delete any group, escalating read-only access to write access across the realm; this contradicts the interface javadoc which says canManage() requires MANAGE.

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2` class, `canManage()` is implemented as:

```java
return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);
```

This means a caller granted only the `VIEW` scope on the (global) groups resource type would satisfy `canManage()` and thus pass `requireManage()`. That escalates view-only permissions into manage permissions at the global level, contradicting the `GroupPermissionEvaluator` javadoc for `canManage()` (which describes manage rights, not view). The defect is directly visible in the diff and is security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The per-user usersEvaluator::canView post-filter was silently removed from searchForUser, replacing it with a group-ID-only session attribute, so user-level (Users resource) VIEW/MANAGE grants no longer contribute to search results. An admin authorized via a permission on an individual user resource (not via any group) previously saw that user in GET /users search; after this change getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns only group-resource grants, the session attribute omits them, and their previously visible users vanish from search results — a silent authorization-surface regression with no accompanying intent statement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably remove the explicit post-filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser`: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` became just `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` (same pattern in `BruteForceUsersResource`). It also changes the restriction mechanism from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` based on group IDs. However, the finding’s specific behavioral claim (that user-level Users-resource VIEW/MANAGE grants no longer contribute and results “vanish”) cannot be proven from this diff alone because the diff does not show whether `toRepresentation(...)` (or the underlying `searchForUserStream`) still enforces `usersEvaluator.canView`/per-user permissions elsewhere. This is a significant, diff-grounded authorization-surface change that warrants verification/tests, but the exact regression described isn’t directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource's own ID) rather than the resource's name (which per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource is the group ID), so the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute is populated with resource IDs, not group IDs. If resource IDs are not identical to group IDs, the downstream search filtering on UserModel.GROUPS matches no real group, and an admin with only VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants sees an empty user list instead of the members of the groups they are authorized for; the same asymmetry is visible in hasPermission(), which looks resources up by name (findByName(server, groupId)) — the write side and read side of this contract use different identifiers.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates resources by type and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set, and also passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(...)`. However, `hasPermission` looks up a resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource` establishes the contract that the *resource name* corresponds to the Keycloak group ID (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`). This means `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is mixing authorization resource IDs with group IDs/resource names, so the returned set is not actually “group IDs with view permission”. Downstream callers set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (e.g., in `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), so populating it with authorization resource IDs can break filtering and yield empty user results for admins who only have VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS via group permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `!auth.users().canView()` guard was dropped, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is now consulted unconditionally, but the empty-set fallthrough means a caller with neither canView nor any group permission still gets no UserModel.GROUPS attribute set and the brute-force user search runs completely unfiltered. A fine-grained-authorized admin with zero granted groups receives the full brute-force user list (all realm users with their brute-force status), the same unrestricted result as a fully privileged admin — the permission narrowing the old code aimed to preserve is silently a no-op for the no-grants case in both old and new code, and this iteration cemented it while touching exactly these lines.

adjudication.rationale: For the “no-grants” case described, the behavior is unchanged by this diff. Previously (in both BruteForceUsersResource and UsersResource) when the caller could not view users, it computed a set via auth.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission() and only set the session attribute if the set was non-empty; if empty, no UserModel.GROUPS attribute was set and the search ran without that narrowing. The new code does the same (computes getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and only sets the session attribute when non-empty). Dropping the !auth.users().canView() guard only adds an unconditional call that returns empty for global viewers; it does not newly create the unfiltered/no-grants outcome the finding claims was introduced/cemented by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The V1 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() shortcut was narrowed from `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()` to `root.users().canView()` only, while every caller of the old method was rewritten in the same diff to call the new one, so the effective contract of all four UsersResource count branches changed without any statement of which behavior was accepted. Admins holding manage-only user permissions (e.g. via MANAGE scope on the Users resource without VIEW) now take the group-scoped path in getUsersCount, and since canView() does not cover them, their counts can silently differ from their pre-change counts; whoever bites this is a fine-grained-authz admin comparing user totals across a Keycloak upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does narrow the shortcut in `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` from `if (root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()) return Collections.emptySet();` to `if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();` (services/.../GroupPermissions.java). In the same PR, all callers (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount` branches and `UsersResource.searchForUser`) were switched from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to the new `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (services/.../UsersResource.java), so the effective behavior of “when do we apply group-scoped filtering/counting” can change. Whether this is an actual bug depends on whether there are real-world cases where `root.users().canManage()` is true while `root.users().canView()` is false, which cannot be proven from this diff alone, but the contract change is real and worth explicitly confirming/documenting/testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check was moved from per-event evaluation to listener-registration time, so the cleanup listener is now permanently bound to the feature state at whatever moment registerListener runs. In any deployment path where registerListener is invoked before feature resolution (or where the feature flag is read from a source that changes between startup and operation), role-removal and group-removal events stop cleaning up the corresponding authorization policies, leaving orphaned permission resources that keep stale grants alive after the originating role/group is deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` moves `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` from inside `onEvent(...)` to guard the `manager.register(...)` call itself. Previously, the listener was always registered and the feature flag was checked per event; now, whether cleanup happens is fixed at registration time. The finding’s broader claim about “feature resolution changing between startup and operation” is not verifiable from the diff, but the underlying review concern (semantic change from per-event to registration-time gating, which would matter if the feature flag could vary after registration) is directly grounded in the shown change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser removes the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` guard and treats an empty group-ids set as full access, so an admin with no view permission at all receives the unscoped user list. An admin holding only query-users (or any role that passes requireQuery but not view) whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (no global canView, no group view-membership grants) now gets every user in the realm returned with full representation, where the old code returned an empty/filtered stream — a direct user-enumeration and PII disclosure bypass of the view-users check.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-user guard `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and also changes the group-scoping logic to always call `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and only set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when that set is non-empty. If a caller lacks global user-view (e.g., has query-only access) and has *no* group view-members/view-membership grants, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` can return an empty set, meaning no `UserModel.GROUPS` attribute is set and the subsequent `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` is passed straight into `toRepresentation(...)` without any `canView` filtering. Compared to the previous code path (which filtered by `usersEvaluator::canView`), this can expose an unscoped user list to a caller who can query but cannot view users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser drops the `if (!auth.users().canView())` gate and any per-result authorization filter, so brute-force status for all realm users is returned whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is empty. An admin without view-users and without any group view-membership grant previously got no results (the GROUPS attribute was only set when permissions existed and canView() gated everything); now the same admin receives the full brute-force status stream including login failure timestamps for every user in the realm.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-result authorization filter: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` becomes just `searchForUserStream(...)` with no `usersEvaluator::canView` filter. At the same time, the only remaining restriction mechanism in this method is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` *only when* `groupIds` is non-empty. Therefore, for an admin who lacks global user view (`usersEvaluator.canView() == false`) and has no group grants (`getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` empty), no restriction is applied before converting to representations, which can expose users (and similarly affects brute-force listing patterns where no per-result filtering is present). This is a correctness/security regression directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canManage() grants manage-level group authority from a VIEW-only scope grant: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` An admin granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource (view-only fine-grained permission, matching canView()'s identical check) is indistinguishable from a MANAGE grant at the canManage() level, so view-only admins can create, update, and delete groups — privilege escalation from view to manage.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns true when the caller has *either* `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` on the (all-)groups resource: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. This makes a VIEW-only grant satisfy a method explicitly named/used for “manage” capability, effectively collapsing VIEW and MANAGE at the global level. Given `GroupPermissionEvaluator`’s contract and typical usage of `canManage()/requireManage()` to gate write operations where no specific group instance exists (e.g., create), this is a privilege escalation risk from view to manage. The diff itself shows the problematic logic in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` and that V2 is now wired via `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission(groupId, ...) evaluates only the group-named resource when one exists, skipping the type-level "all-groups" resource check, so a type-level grant is silently ignored for groups that already have a per-group resource. An admin with MANAGE on all-groups gets Forbidden when managing a group whose per-group resource was previously created (e.g., by an earlier scope permission), while the same grant works for groups without one — the testManageAllGroups case only exercises the no-resource path, so this authorization asymmetry is untested and bites admins inconsistently during rolling permission setups.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, when a per-group `Resource` exists (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns non-null), the method evaluates permissions only against that resource and never considers the type-level "all-groups" resource. The fallback to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (and the check for policies on it) happens only when the per-group resource is missing. Therefore, an admin granted `MANAGE` (or `VIEW`) at the type level can be denied for a group that already has a per-group resource but no corresponding policy granting those scopes. The added `testManageAllGroups` exercises only the fallback path (no per-group resource), so this inconsistent behavior is not covered by tests as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() now returns an empty set for callers lacking canView(), and every caller (UsersResource.getUsersCount, searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) interprets an empty set as "no restriction", making the empty set a dual-meaning sentinel for both full-access and no-access. Any future caller that forgets the separate canView() pre-check gets unrestricted results, and the getUsersCount paths at UsersResource lines 398/425/431 pass the empty set straight into getUsersCount, returning the total realm user count to admins with zero view permission — the count endpoint now leaks realm size where the old getGroupsWithViewPermission-served path denied it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` return `Collections.emptySet()` as a sentinel for “no restriction” when `root.users().canView()` is true (see `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and the interface javadoc). The same method can also legitimately return an empty set when the caller lacks global view and has no per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants (e.g., V2 iterates resources and may add none). Call sites then treat empty as “do nothing” (e.g., `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` only `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` when the set is non-empty; `UsersResource.getUsersCount` passes the set directly into `session.users().getUsersCount(...)`). That dual-meaning empty-set API is a real footgun/design issue created/solidified by this change. However, the finding’s specific claim that the count endpoint now *definitively* leaks total realm size cannot be verified from this diff because the behavior of `session.users().getUsersCount(..., Set<String>)` with an empty set is not shown, and the previous `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` implementation could also return an empty set when no group permissions existed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser drops the `!auth.users().canView()` guard AND removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter, so filtering now depends entirely on the GROUPS session attribute, which is never set when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set. An admin with no view-users role and no group view permissions gets an empty group set, the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set, and searchForUserStream returns the realm's full user list unfiltered — a privilege escalation leaking all users (the old code caught this case with the canView post-filter).

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` (and similarly `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), the diff removes both (a) the `if (!auth.users().canView()) { ... }` guard and (b) the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter. The new logic only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns a non-empty set. If that set is empty (e.g., caller lacks global view and has no group-based view permissions), the code now calls `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` with no subsequent permission filter in this method. The old code would still apply `usersEvaluator::canView` filtering even when no groups attribute was set, preventing accidental over-disclosure. The diff therefore introduces a real risk that the search result is no longer constrained by `usersEvaluator` when the GROUPS session attribute isn't populated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() reuses the empty set as a sentinel with three contradictory meanings: 'caller can view all users' (canView branch), 'cross-realm admin' (returns empty), and 'no groups granted' (loop adds nothing). Callers like UsersResource.getUsersCount (lines 398, 425, 432) cannot distinguish 'unrestricted' from 'restricted to zero groups', so a cross-realm or permission-less admin gets the same empty-set input that a full-view admin gets; the next maintainer of any store provider implementing getUsersCount(realm, Set) will guess the semantics wrong and either leak or over-restrict counts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionEvaluator#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is documented to return `Collections.emptySet()` as a sentinel for “unrestricted” (`if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();` in `GroupPermissions` / `GroupPermissionsV2`), but it also returns an empty set for other cases (`!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, `server == null`, and “no group resources granted” where the `granted` set stays empty). This makes the API contract ambiguous for callers that pass the set downstream (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount(..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())`), because an empty set can mean either “no restriction” or “restricted to zero groups”. The diff doesn’t prove an actual leak/bug in current providers, but it does introduce/retain a concrete, diff-grounded semantic ambiguity that could lead to wrong implementations later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All three getUsersCount call sites changed from getGroupsWithViewPermission to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, but no test in the diff exercises the count endpoints for a group-restricted admin. I checked the test-shaped files in this diff (tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and test-framework ApiUtil.java); neither calls getUsersCount or asserts a count under group-scoped permissions, so a regression in count-vs-search consistency (e.g. count says 5, search returns 1) ships unnoticed to realm admins paging user lists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes three `UsersResource#getUsersCount` branches to pass `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` instead of `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` (e.g. around lines 395–436). However, the added/modified tests in this diff (notably `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) only exercise `users().search(...)` behavior under group-scoped permissions and do not call any user count endpoint or assert count/search consistency for a group-restricted admin. This is a specific coverage gap for newly changed authorization/filtering logic, not a directly verifiable defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 grants user-search visibility (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) only for VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes on group resources, but canView(GroupModel) grants group visibility on VIEW/MANAGE scopes — an admin granted plain VIEW on a group can open that group in the UI yet its members never appear in user searches or counts. An operator who grants 'view' on a group (the natural scope to let someone see a group) silently gets an empty member list via the users endpoint; no test in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest creates a group permission with only VIEW/MANAGE and then asserts users-search behavior, so this inconsistency is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally separates permissions for viewing a group vs viewing its members. `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` checks `VIEW`/`MANAGE` scopes on group resources (group visibility), while member/user visibility is controlled by `canViewMembers`/`canManageMembers` and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, which both use `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` (see `GroupPermissionsV2.canViewMembers` and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`). `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` was changed to rely on `root.groups()::canViewMembers`, aligning user-search visibility with member-view permissions, not group-view permissions. Therefore the finding’s expectation that plain group `VIEW` should make users appear in user searches/counts is not supported by the diff; it misreads the designed permission model rather than exposing a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new switch in getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types, but this new default branch is not triggered by any test in the diff. I checked GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest (the only test file added); it never calls getOrCreateResource with an invalid resourceType, so a regression that maps a valid type string into the default branch (e.g. a typo'd constant) would surface as a raw 500 to admin clients instead of being caught by a test asserting the intended error contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource`, the PR replaces an if/else chain with a `switch (resourceType)` that now has a `default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Resource type [" + resourceType + "] not found.")`. In the previous code, an unknown `resourceType` would leave `name` unset and then fall into the subsequent `if (name == null)` path (throwing a different exception type). The newly added test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` only exercises valid types/scopes and never drives the `default` branch, so the changed behavior for unexpected/mismapped `resourceType` strings is untested and could surface as a raw 500/error-contract change without a regression test catching it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved from inside the ProviderEventListener to wrap the listener registration entirely — a behavioral change on the feature-disabled path with no test in the diff exercising a feature-disabled server. I checked GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest and KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig usage in the diff — every test runs with the feature enabled (the config class exists precisely to enable it), so if the hoisted check accidentally reads the profile before bootstrap completes (returning false and silently skipping listener registration), stale group permission resources would never be cleaned up on role/group deletion and no test would notice.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior: in AdminPermissions.registerListener the feature flag check is hoisted to wrap listener registration (now the listener is not registered at all when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled), whereas before it was always registered but would no-op in onEvent when the feature was disabled. The added/modified tests (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest annotated with KeycloakIntegrationTest(config = KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig.class)) only run with the feature enabled, so this altered feature-disabled path and any potential initialization/registration edge cases are not exercised by tests in this diff. The specific bootstrap-timing failure mode described is speculative beyond what the diff proves, so this is more of a coverage/behavioral-change concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants full group management to callers holding only the VIEW scope, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) instead of MANAGE alone. An admin granted a view-only all-groups permission can create, update, and delete groups and map roles to them (GroupResource/GroupsResource only call canManage/canView before mutating), an authorization bypass versus the documented contract that canManage requires the MANAGE scope — note the per-group canManage(GroupModel) overload correctly checks only MANAGE, so the global and per-group paths disagree.

[BUG] searchForUser removes the application-level `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and relies entirely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute being honored by the user provider, but the attribute is only set when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns non-empty. For a group-scoped admin whose user storage provider does not implement the GROUPS attribute filter (any custom/UserStorageProvider federation that ignores unknown attributes), searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm with no downstream permission filter, exposing users the admin has no permission to view; previously the stream-level canView filter caught this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably remove the explicit application-level permission filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser` (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now relies on optionally setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` before calling `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` (same pattern also applied in `BruteForceUsersResource`). However, the finding’s claim that there is “no downstream permission filter” cannot be confirmed from the diff because the implementation of `toRepresentation(...)` is not shown here and may still enforce `usersEvaluator` checks. What is grounded in the diff is the increased reliance on the user provider honoring the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute for pre-filtering; reviewers should ensure permissions are still enforced even if a user provider ignores that attribute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission() looks up per-group resources via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), but pre-existing fine-grained group resources in upgraded realms are named with the V1 convention "group.resource.<id>" (GroupPermissions.getGroupResourceName), so the lookup by raw group id misses them. Realms upgraded from the V1 admin-fine-grained-authz model silently lose their existing per-group permission grants when evaluated through V2 (hasPermission falls through to the all-groups policy and returns false), so admins who could manage specific groups are locked out with no error, warning, or migration/backfill step for renaming resources.

adjudication.rationale: In the new V2 evaluator, `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up a per-group `Resource` via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e. expecting the resource *name* to be the raw group id. However, the existing (V1) group permissions code in this diff clearly uses a different naming convention (`GroupPermissions.RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."` and `getGroupResourceName(group) -> "group.resource." + group.getId()`). The diff does not show any compatibility lookup (e.g., trying both `groupId` and `group.resource.<id>`), migration, or backfill. Therefore, if a realm has pre-existing per-group resources created under the V1 naming, V2 evaluation would fail to find them and fall back to the all-groups resource path, potentially returning false and denying previously granted access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new code sets the GROUPS attribute unconditionally (whenever non-empty) instead of only when auth.users().canView() is false, and it drops the canView gate entirely from the search path. For callers who can view all users, the GROUPS attribute is now set on the session only when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() happens to return entries (e.g., V2 admins holding an explicit all-groups VIEW permission), narrowing the brute-force user search to that group list even though the caller has realm-wide view rights — a behavior change on the same request path with no V1/V2 distinction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit `if (!auth.users().canView())` wrapper, but the new helper `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is defined (in `GroupPermissionEvaluator`/`GroupPermissions`/`GroupPermissionsV2`) to return an empty set when the caller can view users (`if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();`). Therefore, for callers with realm-wide user view rights, `groupIds` will be empty and `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` will not be set at all, so the claimed narrowing of the search for such callers is not supported by the diff. Also, while `UsersResource.searchForUser` drops a `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`, the diff does not show the full downstream enforcement (`toRepresentation` / user storage behavior), so the claim that the canView gate is “dropped entirely” cannot be verified from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter makes the search stream completely unfiltered whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (caller lacks users().canView() AND has no group view-members grants). An admin holding only the query-users role (who previously got an empty, permission-filtered result) now receives full UserRepresentations of every user in the realm, including emails and attributes — a silent exposure of data the previous code guaranteed was filtered, with no error raised.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the explicit permission filter: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced by an unfiltered `searchForUserStream(...)` (and likewise in `BruteForceUsersResource`). The only remaining restriction mechanism shown in the diff is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. If a caller lacks global `users().canView()` and also has no group member-view grants, `groupIds` will be empty, the session attribute is not set, and the stream passed to `toRepresentation(...)` is unfiltered. From the diff alone, there is no other filtering step introduced to compensate, so this can expose users that previously would have been removed by the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten searchForUser drops the authorization narrowing entirely: when groupIds is empty (no view-users and no group permissions) the UserModel.GROUPS attribute is never set, yet searchForUserStream is invoked with no subsequent permission filter, returning every realm user. A brute-force listing endpoint served to an admin without user-view permission returns all users' brute-force status unfiltered, where the old code constrained results via the group permission attribute path — silent over-visibility with a success response.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit authorization narrowing `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now always returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly (after optionally setting `UserModel.GROUPS` only when `groupIds` is non-empty). If the caller cannot globally view users and `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set, no session attribute is set and no subsequent permission filter is applied in this method, so the stream can include users the caller cannot view. The previous code’s filter would have prevented this even when the group set was empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource's internal ID) instead of the group ID (the resource name, which the sibling hasPermission() lookup `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` confirms is the group ID) into the granted set. The collected IDs are set as the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and compared against real group IDs during user search, so an admin granted view-members on specific groups gets a set of unmatched resource UUIDs and the user-search filter silently matches nothing — the admin sees zero users despite valid permissions, with no error or log.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates authz `Resource` objects and uses `groupResource.getId()` both for the permission check (`hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`) and for the returned set (`granted.add(groupResource.getId())`). However, `hasPermission()` looks up group resources via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, implying the *name* is the group identifier (and `AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`, i.e., the real group id). Using the authorization resource internal id (UUID) therefore won’t match `findByName`, and the returned set will contain internal resource IDs, not real group IDs. This set is then placed into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` in `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource`, so downstream filtering that expects real group IDs will silently not match, causing users to be hidden despite valid group-member-view permissions.
